name: merks-ecm-reciprocity-2d
title: Cell-ECM mechanical reciprocity (Merks 3D CPM-ECM, 2D real-engine reproduction — FAILS: coupling gap)
lead:
The 3D target paper has no public code and runs on a GPU/HPC cluster. Rather
than reimplement it, this investigation bridges the actual published 2D
engine it descends from (Tsingos 2023) and runs it on a laptop via Docker,
then asks how much of the 3D paper's story the real 2D ancestor reproduces.
The honest answer: the mechanisms reproduce clearly; the quantitative
equilibrium figures need model calibration that is documented, not faked.

at_a_glance.role: FAILS the coupling bar. The cell contracts (13000->~0) but its adhesion ring stays frozen (~58 px) across every regime tried — the cell detaches from the ECM instead of dragging it inward (q/q0 only ~1.09, densification ~0). The paper's Fig-4 remodeling is NOT reproduced. (A real bridge bug — float settings written as ints — was found + fixed while investigating.)

FAILS the percolation bar. Crosslinking raises the giant component from 0.0007 to ~0.30 but it SATURATES there — the network never percolates (~1.0) at CPU-tractable densities, so the paper's Fig-2B mechanical regime is not reached. The connectivity ONSET is reproduced; full percolation is not.

how_to_read:
Start with the verdict above. Each study's interactive figure is built from
REAL engine output (no synthetic data). 'Mechanism-confirmed' means the
direction/qualitative behavior matches the paper; it is deliberately NOT a
claim of quantitative figure reproduction. The two 'evidence_against' points
and the calibration gap are the honest limits, not footnotes.

glossary.definition: The real 2D hybrid cellular Potts + bead-spring ECM engine (Tsingos et al. 2023), TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3. Bridged by viva-tstmd and run CPU-only via Docker.
Cells deform/remodel the ECM while the ECM's mechanics shape the cell — the mutual coupling this investigation reproduces.
Fraction of fibers nearly radial to the cell (alignment gamma>=0.9, paper eq. 7) over its initial value; >1 means fibers reorient toward the cell.
Fraction of ECM beads in the largest connected component of the bond+crosslink graph; a percolation measure (paper Fig 2B).

The quantitative equilibrium figures (Fig 2 magnitude, Fig 3) are not reproduced because mapping the authors' physical-unit parameters to the engine's internal units is unsolved here. Documented, not tuned away.

biological_story:
Cells and the extracellular matrix (ECM) are in constant mechanical dialogue.
A cell anchors to the surrounding fiber network through adhesions and pulls:
the ECM resists, deforms, and remembers — fibers reorient toward the cell and
the matrix densifies locally. That resistance in turn shapes how far the cell
can contract or spread. This mutual push-and-pull, "mechanical reciprocity,"
is how tissues set their form in development, wound healing, and cancer
invasion.

The stiffness of the matrix is not a fixed material constant — it is built by
crosslinks that tie neighboring collagen fibers together. Below a critical
crosslink density the network is a loose collection of disconnected strands
that a cell can rearrange freely; above it, the fibers form a single connected
(percolated) scaffold that transmits force over long range and genuinely
resists the cell. Crosslinking is thus the knob that converts a floppy gel
into a load-bearing tissue.

This investigation watches that dialogue directly in a real simulator: a
contractile cell embedded in a crosslinked bead-spring ECM. We see the cell
contract and drag nearby fibers into radial alignment (reorientation), and we
see crosslinking knit the loose network into a connected scaffold (the onset
of percolation) — the two sides of the reciprocity the Merks-lab models were
built to study.
question:
Can we reproduce the cell-ECM mechanical-reciprocity phenomena of Keijzer &
Merks 2026 (arXiv:2609.02375, a 3D hybrid cellular Potts model coupled to a
discrete deformable fiber network — code unreleased) by driving the REAL
published 2D ancestor engine (Tsingos et al. 2023 static-adhesion TST-MD)
on ordinary hardware?
hypothesis:
The 3D paper extends a published, open 2D engine. Bridged and run CPU-only,
that real engine should reproduce — at the mechanism level, in 2D — the same
reciprocity phenomena: a contractile cell deforms a crosslinked bead-spring
ECM, fibers reorient toward the cell (q/q0 > 1), and crosslinking builds
network connectivity (percolation).

acceptance_criteria.behavior: FAILS. Paper bar: the contracting cell drags its adhesions + the crosslinked ECM inward (adhesion-ring radius shrinks with the cell; strong reorientation + densification). Measured: adhesion ring stays ~58 px while area 13000->~0; q/q0 only ~1.09; densification ~0. The cell-ECM coupling does not engage in any regime tried.

FAILS. Paper bar (Fig 2B): the giant component percolates (>=0.8) at high crosslinking. Measured: it saturates at ~0.30 and never percolates at CPU-tractable densities. The connectivity onset is reproduced; full percolation is not.

executive.what_is_this:
A real-engine, 2D reproduction of the mechanical-reciprocity phenomena in a
recent (unreleased) 3D cell-ECM model from the Merks lab. The deliverable
has two parts: (1) viva-tstmd — a reusable process-bigraph bridge that runs
the genuine TST-MD simulator (TST C++ + HOOMD + MUSCLE3) CPU-only inside
Docker, with 19 tests; and (2) this investigation, which uses it to measure
the paper's observables on real runs. The reproduction currently FAILS its
paper-faithful bars — the study tests are intentionally left failing until
the cell-ECM coupling and percolation issues are resolved.
executive.verdict:
NOT REPRODUCED. The infrastructure goal is met — viva-tstmd runs the genuine
engine CPU-only — but the paper's core cell-ECM mechanical reciprocity does
NOT reproduce in this engine build at tractable scale. Both studies FAIL
their paper-faithful acceptance bars. The tests are intentionally left
failing until the underlying issues are fixed.

Where it fails (measured on real runs, every regime tried):
  * Coupling — a contracting cell does NOT drag its adhesions / the
    crosslinked ECM inward. The adhesion ring stays frozen (~58 px) while the
    cell contracts 13000 -> ~0; the cell detaches from the ECM. q/q0 reaches
    only ~1.09 and densification ~0 — far from the paper's Fig-4 remodeling.
  * Percolation — the fiber network never percolates: the giant component
    saturates at ~0.30 (bar >=0.8) even at ~13000 crosslinks, so the Fig-2B
    mechanical regime is not reached.

What was established along the way (honest sub-results): the engine genuinely
runs and the cell contracts; crosslinking raises connectivity from a
disconnected network (the Fig-2B onset); and a REAL bridge bug (float-typed
settings written as ints, which silently crashed every varied-stiffness run)
was found + fixed. The coupling search exhausted the exposed parameters
(fiber stiffness, density, crosslinking, contractility lambda, md_kT,
adhesion-annihilation penalty, gradient/uniform displacement selection)
without engaging the dragging mechanism.

Likely cause: reproducing the coupled pulling needs the authors' exact
(undocumented) configuration or deeper engine work — the adhesion-retraction
mechanism is not dragging adhesions through any ymmsl-exposed knob. No
constant was tuned to fake a fit.

decisions_needed.context: ca.cpp:575 rounds the ECM work to int, erasing sub-unit resistance. Engine instrumentation confirmed adhesions DO move (sync works); the blocker is bistability. See study followup_proposals FP-01 and docs/cell-ecm-coupling.md.

decisions_needed.question: Implement physical->internal unit-scaling (Frontiers Table 1, K=Y*A/L) so adh_dh grows with fiber stretch and escapes bistability?
decisions_needed.context: The drag->densify->stiffen feedback never ignites because resistance is ~constant. This is the principled fix that should also recover Fig 2/3 magnitudes. See FP-02.

decisions_needed.context: The paper's contraction-experiment parameters are not in the public code/docs. See FP-03.

decisions_needed.context: Giant component saturates ~0.30 at CPU-tractable sizes. See tstmd-network-connectivity FP-01/FP-02.

scientific_argument.main_claim: The real published 2D engine, bridged and run on a laptop, does NOT reproduce the 3D paper's cell-ECM mechanical reciprocity at tractable scale: the cell detaches from its adhesions rather than dragging the ECM in, and the network never percolates. Both studies fail their paper-faithful bars; tests are left failing until fixed.
evidence_for: The engine is the REAL TST-MD (not a reimplementation/mock); the cell genuinely contracts and crosslinking raises connectivity (the Fig-2B onset).
A real bridge bug (float settings written as ints) was found + fixed, unblocking the full parameter search.
evidence_against: Coupling FAILS: adhesion-ring radius stays ~58 px while the cell contracts 13000 -> ~0 — the cell detaches from the ECM in every regime (q/q0 only ~1.09, densification ~0).
Percolation FAILS: giant component saturates at ~0.30 (bar >=0.8), never reaching the paper's connected regime.
Every exposed parameter (stiffness, density, crosslinking, lambda, md_kT, annihilation penalty, displacement selection) was swept without engaging the dragging mechanism.
key_figures: tstmd-contraction-reorientation: contraction + q/q0 time series with start/end ECM snapshots.
tstmd-network-connectivity: giant component vs crosslinks created.
caveats: 2D (engine) vs 3D (target paper): mechanism/direction analog, not a dimensional match.
Static adhesions (as the 3D paper uses), not the dynamic focal adhesions of Keijzer 2025.
Reduced sizes for CPU tractability; single seed per condition.
Quantitative equilibrium figures (Fig 2 magnitude, Fig 3) require unit-scaling calibration — not attempted/claimed here.

findings.statement: The real TST-MD engine does NOT reproduce the paper's cell-ECM coupling. Engine instrumentation (rebuilt bin/adhesions, logged AdhesionMover) shows the CPM DOES move adhesions (876 commits, ~1.27px/frame) and the CPM->MD sync works — so it is NOT a sync bug. The obstruction is BISTABILITY: the ECM resistance adh_dh is ~constant (fibers aren't dragged -> no densification -> no stiffening feedback), so the engine only ever fully holds the cell (lambda<=3, no contraction) or lets it collapse leaving the adhesions behind (lambda>=4), even at 2000 MCS with gradient selection. No drag-to-new-equilibrium regime is reachable from any ymmsl parameter. See followup_proposals + viva-tstmd/docs/cell-ecm-coupling.md.

What DOES hold (sub-reproduction): the cell genuinely contracts (13000 -> ~0) and shows weak reorientation (q/q0 ~1.09). But these are not the paper's remodeling result; densification stays ~0. A real bridge bug (float-typed settings written as ints) was found + fixed while investigating, which unblocked the parameter search.

studies.question: Does the real 2D bead-spring ECM engine reproduce the paper's network percolation (Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 2B) — the giant component rising to a fully connected (~1.0) network at high crosslinking, the regime in which the matrix mechanically resists and transmits cell forces long-range?

findings.statement: The real engine does NOT reproduce the paper's percolated network at CPU-tractable sizes: the giant component saturates at ~0.30 and never approaches full percolation (~1.0). The connectivity onset is reproduced; the percolated regime is not.

Sub-reproduction that DOES hold: crosslinking sharply raises connectivity from a disconnected network (0.0007 -> 0.18 at the first crosslinks) — the onset direction of Fig 2B. Reaching full percolation likely needs near-paper-scale densities beyond what runs CPU-tractably here.
